To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed ICD-10 and ICD-11 criteria for PTSD and CPTSD are supported by the data.
the latent profile analysis (LPA) of PTSD and Complex PTSD (CPTSD) symptom profiles revealed a three-profile solution.
the proposed ICD- 11 diagnoses of PTSD and complex PTSD are empirically distinct and that the proposed ICS-11 diagnosis of complex PTSD is a distinct latent class.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of an innovative approach to the treatment of PTSD in adults and children.
the development of a new diagnostic category, complex posttraumatic stress disorder, for inclusion in ICD-11.
the development of a new, more complex, and more comprehensive model of PTSD, which we call complex PTSD (CPTSD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is not yet strong enough for PTSD and complex PTSD to be classified as separate disorders in ICD-11.

the evidence supports the inclusion of complex post-traumatic stress disorder (CPTSD) in the ICD-11, and the proposed ICD-10 diagnostic criteria for CPTSD (including the 2-factor structure of PTSD and CPTSD) is supported by a substantial body of research.
the proposed ICD- 11 PTSD and complex trauma disorders are not supported by evidence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found support for the validity of the proposed ICD- 11 PTSD and CPTSD diagnoses.
the proposed ICD-10 PTSD and complex PTSD (CPTSD) are supported as latent classes in the general population.
the proposed ICD-10/11 PTSD and complex-PTSD categories are not empirically distinguishable from one another and from a third category that we have labelled as 'traumatic exposure' (TE).
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to develop and validate measures of PTSD and C-PTSD that are more specific to these two disorders.
we can use machine learning methods to predict the onset of PTSD symptoms in a population of people exposed to trauma.
we need to be careful about how we talk about trauma.
